mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of future earnings and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for ≥2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.6%, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations, which compresses equity real returns and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In regimes where ΔCPIAUCSL > 0.6%, SPX 20-day forward returns are positive at >80% frequency (Kolmogorov-Smirnov p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) signals a strong labor market, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by ≥0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 5 consecutive months of such labor market conditions, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a neutral baseline (Mann-Whitney U p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 2% for three consecutive months indicates improving supply-side capacity, which reduces output gap compression and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO grows ≥2% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During such supply expansions, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in monthly HOUST (housing starts) by at least 15% in two consecutive months suggests cooling demand, which raises discount rates and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by ≥15% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: In cooling periods, SPX 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-cooling baselines (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for four consecutive months while UNRATE stays above 5%, the low-rate/low-unemployment environment sustains optimism about future growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4% for 4 consecutive months AND UNRATE > 5%
failure_condition: During such regimes, SPX 60-day forward returns are not superior to a neutral 1% risk-free benchmark (Sharpe ratio < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in RSAFS (retail sales) by more than 8% in a single month followed by a sustained monthly decline in PAYEMS of at least 5% indicates softening consumer demand, which compresses earnings expectations and predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >8% in one month AND PAYEMS falls by ≥5% in the following month
regime_hint: early signs of consumer demand weakness
failure_condition: In such demand weakness regimes, SPX 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (Kolmogorov-Smirnov p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in GDPC1 (GDP chained price parity) of at least 3% while INDPRO remains flat suggests a contraction in real activity, raising discount rates and forecasting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls ≥3% for 2 consecutive months AND INDPRO does not increase
failure_condition: During such output contractions, SPX 5-day forward returns are not more negative than during neutral GDP growth (t-test p > 0.1).
